rules: SF Rent Board · rent increase guide

index: A cautious path, not a market reset.

Consider no increase or a modest annual-only increase up to the published 1.6%, after all eligibility checks. This is a conservative research recommendation, not a legal opinion or evidence of market norms.
1.6% of lawful base rent for covered units; effective March 1, 2026–February 28, 2027. It is an allowance, not a mandatory increase and not a universal cap on every type of approved adjustment.
$3,995 × 0.016 = $63.92/month; illustrative new rent $4,058.92. Supplied base is unverified. No banked increase included; not an authorized amount.
$3,150 × 0.016 = $50.40/month; illustrative new rent $3,200.40. The 2019 rent is not confirmed as today’s lawful base. No banked increase included.
Do not treat these illustrations as notices. Confirm coverage, lawful rent history, anniversary, lease permission, current license, service method, and discrimination/retaliation issues first.

Applying the same neutral annual-review policy to both is recommended; actual dates and outcomes may differ. Raising both does not immunize discrimination, and raising only one is not by itself proof of it. Review the reasons and facts, not just numerical equality.
This is source-based legal information, not a tenant-lawyer review, litigation guarantee, or exhaustive title/lease audit. No lawyer has reviewed either proposed increase.

No names, initials, address, parcel, contact details, or identity key are stored in this site. Dates and amounts remain as supplied. Their combination can still create re-identification risk; this public site is not a confidential file store.

A first annual increase generally requires 12 months after the lease began. The supplied February 1, 2025 date is not a verified eligibility date. The April 2026 household change does not itself authorize a roommate surcharge or market reset. Review leases and actual occupancy.
Do not assume no increases since 2019 from an old lease figure. Current lawful base, last increase and banked entitlement remain blank until the complete ledger and notices are reviewed.

At 1.6%, Unit 1 illustration: +$63.92 monthly / +$767.04 over 12 full months. Unit 2 illustration: +$50.40 monthly / +$604.80 over 12 full months. Combined +$114.32 monthly / +$1,371.84 over 12 full months; not a calendar-year revenue forecast.
Actual proposed effective date for each unit: blank. Do not assume a 2027 rate beyond February 28, 2027 from the current posting.
law: Local protection comes first for covered units.
Many units built on or before June 13, 1979 have local rent control, but exceptions and classification matter. A reported 1940 construction date alone does not establish coverage.

Apply the published percentage effective on the increase date to base rent, including housing services such as parking/storage; exclude temporary passthroughs and fluctuating charges. Do not round up to a whole dollar.
First annual increase generally after 12 months; subsequent annual increases at least 12 months apart. A delayed increase changes the anniversary date.

Civil Code §1947.12(a) sets the state cap at the lesser of 5% plus cost-of-living change or 10% for covered property. Subdivision (d)(3) exempts housing under a valid, lower local rent cap. Do not substitute the larger state formula for SF’s covered-unit allowance.

The Fair Housing Act prohibits housing discrimination based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status and disability. HUD’s cited overview establishes protections, not a numeric SF rent allowance. Subsidy-program status is unverified here.

CRD identifies broader state protections, reasonable accommodation obligations and prohibitions on retaliation for exercising fair housing rights. Ownership size does not establish immunity from these rules; exemptions need fact-specific review.
An additional or replacement roommate moving in with an existing tenant is not itself a lawful reason for additional rent, even if a lease says otherwise.

Properly banked percentages are added, not compounded or prorated. Skipped increases generally require at least 24 full months without an increase to bank; partial unused increases have separate rules. Anniversary changes can lose an increase. No banked total is established here.

Capital improvements, operating/maintenance and other adjustments have distinct petition/worksheet rules. Cost increases do not automatically authorize an arbitrary surcharge; review the applicable process and approval before collection.
Official-confirmed typical increase for Outer Sunset 94122: blank. The cited annual allowance is a city rent-control rule, not a neighborhood market survey or a requirement to reach market rent.

Civil Code §1942.5 addresses rent increases in retaliation for habitability complaints, tenant organizing and lawful exercise of rights. Its 180-day provisions have conditions and exceptions; do not treat timing alone as automatic legal clearance or automatic liability.
practice: Official-confirmed usual SF corporate increase percentage and frequency: blank. The reviewed official sources do not establish what corporations typically charge; no industry norm is asserted.
Official-confirmed usual SF small-owner increase percentage and frequency: blank. No claim that individual owners always increase annually, skip years, or use a particular percentage.
Suggested business process · either owner type

Maintain a rent ledger, conduct a documented annual eligibility review, use the published allowance, verify the license and retain the served notice/service record. This is a recommended workflow, not a verified survey of owner behavior.

Use the annual allowable adjustment as the legal basis if eligible. If explaining budget pressures, use only actual documented insurance, repairs, taxes or operating costs; do not claim those costs establish a right to exceed the allowance. Do not invent expenses.

Different legal anniversaries, fixed-term lease constraints or documented decisions to defer may justify different outcomes. These are possible neutral explanations, not established facts about these households or a legal safe harbor.

Prefer the same review criteria and, when appropriate, the same percentage rather than an equal dollar increase. Do not increase a second unit merely to conceal discriminatory treatment of the first. Record genuine reasons for any difference.

A tenant reviewer should challenge the base rent, omitted credits/services, percentage date, prior increases, banked ledger and any unapproved passthrough. The calculation alone does not prove legality.

Review complaints, accommodation requests, protected activity and timing privately with counsel. A small increase can still be discriminatory or retaliatory; uniform increases do not cure unlawful motives. Do not profile tenants or collect protected characteristics for pricing.

The City directs tenants with rent increase notices to tenant counseling organizations and tenants with eviction court papers to immediate free legal help. This does not verify free individual lawyer review of every routine rent notice.
notice: Preparation guidance — not a notice to serve.
Check property classification, actual lease term and any limits on mid-term increases. Lease end dates and clauses are unverified; do not treat an annual allowance as overriding a fixed-term promise.
Review the complete ledger, lease amendments, discounts, notices and last effective increase. No tenant-specific lawful base or anniversary has been certified here.

Have a current rent increase license on file when an annual/banked increase becomes effective. Inventory reporting is due March 1 annually; submission data is public. The license need not be attached to the notice.

At least 30 days written notice for increases of 10% or less; 90 days if greater than 10%, counting combined increases during the preceding 12 months. More notice does not make an excessive increase lawful.

Civil Code §827 provides personal delivery or mail under Code of Civil Procedure §1013. SF guidance adds five days for mailing; confirm §1013’s applicable extension if mailing outside California. Do not rely on email or text alone.

Include dollar increase, percentage and effective date. Identify any banked portion. For clarity include current lawful base, resulting rent and unit identification in the private served document, never the public dashboard.

If true: “This is an annual allowable base-rent adjustment using the SF Rent Board percentage effective on the stated date.” Add verified calculation, required notice dates and a contact for questions. This sentence is not a completed statutory notice.

Retain leases/amendments, complete rent ledger, prior notices and service evidence, current/historical licenses, calculation, banking records if claimed, relevant orders and documented neutral rationale. Have qualified SF counsel review unresolved issues before service.
No notices have been served, rents changed, filings made, or legal approval obtained by this project. The research dashboard cannot certify unavailable private records.
flagged: Official-confirmed construction year, legal unit type and rent-control coverage: blank. Supplied 1940 and covered status are not independent verification. Resolve with property records and Rent Board classification, not public tenant details.
Official-confirmed current lawful base, prior increases, service components and banked entitlement for both units: blank. A lease amount is not a complete rent history.
Unit 1 continuing occupancy and April 1, 2026 amendment terms are unverified. Do not assume a vacancy reset or an automatic new anniversary from a roommate change.
Current licenses, lease end dates, increase clauses, restrictions, subsidy terms and any Rent Board orders: blank. These are implementation gates, not reasons to prevent publication of this research.
Official-confirmed Outer Sunset typical increase, corporate typical increase and individual-owner typical increase: blank. Legal allowance is not evidence of actual market behavior.
Actual tenant-lawyer review and a guarantee of no discrimination claim: blank. No legal outcome can be promised from these facts.

The SF rent guide’s one-year example labels June 1, 2025 as 1.6% although its stated 2026 calculation and announcement apply 1.6% to 2026. The banked guide also has an August 2024/2025 date mismatch in its example. Use explicit effective-period announcements and review examples carefully.

Dates and amounts remain public as requested; household labels replace all personal identifiers. Combinations of dates, rents and area can still be identifying. No public identity mapping or private leases are included.

Official pages were retrieved November 6, 2026. Links are for manual review; content can change. No exhaustive case-law search, authenticated property record review or independent legal opinion was performed.
